sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Iredell County?
sections.html:
Iredell County Tax Administration runs the whole property tax system from its building at 135 E. Water Street in Statesville, and it is split into an assessor division, a tax collector division and a land records mapping division. The county board of commissioners set the policy, but you deal with the staff for almost everything.

The county Tax Administration page lists the office as open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The assessor line is 704-878-3017 and the collector line is 704-878-3020. Mail goes to PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687.

  • Assessor division: listing, values, exemptions and appeals.
  • Tax collector division: bills, payments, delinquent accounts and closing payoffs.
  • Land records mapping: parcel maps and the online GIS used to find an owner of record.

If you are selling a house in Iredell County, you will usually talk to the collector about the bill and to the assessor about a value you disagree with.

sections.h2: What is the Iredell County property tax rate?
sections.html:
The county rate is 0.50 per $100 of assessed value for the 2026 tax year, the same figure the county printed for 2025 and 2024. The commissioners kept that rate in the 2026-2027 budget they approved.

Your bill adds a municipal rate if you live inside a town, plus any fire or special district. The table below shows the 2026 column from the county tax rates page, with every figure per $100 of assessed value.

The county also bills a flat solid waste fee of $64 per household, mobile home or apartment for 2026, and half of that for an owner with the elderly or disabled exclusion. Davidson adds a $20 privilege charge on vehicles, and Mooresville has its own solid waste fee.

sections.h2: When are Iredell County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills go out in August and are due September 1, but you can pay through January 5 without penalty. Interest of 2 percent applies on January 6, and another 0.75 percent is added on the first of each month after that.

North Carolina law sets the same framework for every county. The listing period runs the month of January, and the statute on due dates and interest explains the January 6 trigger. A town or county may also adopt a prepayment discount, so ask the collector whether one applies to the unit you are in.

Iredell also advertises unpaid real estate taxes in the newspaper during March and adds an advertising fee to the bill. The collector lists these tools for a delinquent account:

  • Attachment of bank accounts
  • Debt set-off against state income tax refunds
  • Garnishment of wages or rents
  • Levy on rents or other money owed to you
  • Seizure of a vehicle or other personal property
  • Foreclosure

Motor vehicle tax is separate. It rides on the state tag renewal notice and is paid to the Division of Motor Vehicles, not the county office.

sections.h2: How does reappraisal work in Iredell County?
sections.html:
Iredell County reappraises every four years, which is twice as often as the state minimum of eight. The last effective date was January 1, 2023, and the county rate table says the next revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027.

The county has published an adopted schedule of values for 2027 on its assessor pages, and the commissioners have discussed preparation for the countywide reappraisal at recent meetings. State law at G.S. 105-286 sets the outside limit, and a county can choose a shorter cycle.

Appraisers group the county into neighborhoods, review recent sales in each one and adjust values to market. They screen out sales that do not reflect market value, such as transfers between relatives, gifts and trades. A sale made under pressure can also pull a price down, which is one reason the county does not rely on every closing it sees.

For a seller, a reappraisal year matters because the value on the notice becomes the base for tax bills until the next reappraisal. If you plan to list a home around a revaluation date, look up the new appraisal card on the county taxweb site before you set a price.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Iredell County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with an informal appeal to the assessor within 30 days of the date on your Notice of Real Estate Assessed Value, then go to the Board of Equalization and Review if you still disagree. The county page spells out each step.

  1. Complete the appeal form with your evidence and send it to the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, or file it online. An appraiser reviews it and mails a new notice.
  2. If you are still unhappy, appeal in writing to the Board of Equalization and Review, before its adjournment date or within 30 days of the last notice.
  3. The board mails its decision within 30 days after the hearing.
  4. Appeal to the state Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the board notice date.

The county says the board's formal request must be in writing, must name the grounds and the property, and must be signed by the owner or an attorney. Appeals to the board are not accepted electronically, though the first-stage assessor appeal can be filed online. A representative who is not an owner or attorney must attach a power of attorney, or the appeal may be rejected. Under G.S. 105-322 the board first meets between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May.

At a valuation hearing the county's appraisal is presumed correct, so you carry the burden of proof. Send evidence with the appeal or at least 10 working days before the hearing. The county lists these as valid grounds:

  • The assessed value is not comparable to market value on the reappraisal date.
  • The assessment is not equitable compared with similar properties.
  • There are errors on the property record card.

Reasons the county says will not win include inability to pay, high taxes, low county services and market changes after the reappraisal date.

sections.h2: What property tax relief is available in Iredell County?
sections.html:
North Carolina has three homestead programs, and an owner can use only one of them. All three are filed with the county assessor on Form AV-9, not with the state.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: owner is 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with income at or under $38,800 for 2026 under the state form. The excluded amount is the greater of $25,000 or half of the home's appraised value.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: taxes capped at 4 percent of income up to the limit and 5 percent up to $58,200, for owners who have lived in the home five years.

The state AV-9 form says applications are taken through June 1 before the tax year. Under the circuit breaker, deferred tax becomes due if you sell or stop using the home as your residence, so a seller in that program should ask the assessor for the payoff amount before closing.

Present-use value assessment for farm and forest land, and builder inventory exclusions, are also handled by the assessor division.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when I sell a house in Iredell County?
sections.html:
The seller is liable for the full year's bill when the house sells after January 1, because ownership for tax purposes is set on that date. The split between buyer and seller is a private matter handled at closing.

The collector tells owners that a transfer does not relieve the seller of the tax, that the seller receives the bill for the year of transfer, and that proration is a contract between the parties. The county suggests asking your realtor or closing attorney how it was prorated. If you want no loose ends, you can request that the payment be made to the collector at closing, and the office will take a prepayment based on the previous year's rate if the current bill is not out yet.

Back taxes are the bigger concern. A tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date under G.S. 105-355, so a buyer's attorney will want the account current. Iredell advertises the owner of record on the delinquency date, so ask the collector for a payoff before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What does Iredell County look like by the numbers?
sections.html:
Iredell County had an estimated 211,798 residents on July 1, 2025, up 13.5 percent from the April 2020 base, according to Census QuickFacts. It covers 574.41 square miles of land and has about 93,711 housing units.

  • Owner-occupied housing rate for 2020 to 2024: 71.9 percent
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $321,400
  • Median household income: $81,419
  • Median gross rent: $1,252
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,835

The county includes Statesville, Mooresville, Troutman, Davidson, Harmony and Love Valley, and each taxes at its own rate on top of the county's. Commuters average 25.1 minutes to work.

faqs.q: What is the Iredell County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is .50 per $100 for 2026, and Statesville, Mooresville and other towns add their own rates. Check the county rates page for your town and fire district.

faqs.q: When must Iredell County taxes be paid?
faqs.a: Bills are due September 1 and are penalty free through January 5. Interest of 2 percent starts January 6, then 0.75 percent more each month.

faqs.q: Where do I file an appeal in Iredell County?
faqs.a: File first with the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, within 30 days of your value notice. A second-level appeal goes in writing to the Board of Equalization and Review, and a third to the state Property Tax Commission.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when I sell in Iredell County?
faqs.a: The seller is billed for the year of sale if the house sells after January 1, and proration with the buyer is settled in the contract or at closing. You can ask to pay the collector at closing.

faqs.q: Is there tax relief for older owners in Iredell County?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, may qualify for the elderly or disabled exclusion if income is within the limit, and the state caps the application at June 1. The county also halves the solid waste fee for those owners.
